subject: Mythology
title: The Golem: A Monster Made from Clay
description: A quick, practical guide to The Golem: A Monster Made from Clay.

hook.text: A rabbi in Prague built a giant man from clay and brought it to life with a sacred word to protect his people.

buildup.text: The Jewish community faced violent persecution. Rabbi Loew shaped the Golem and wrote 'emet' (truth) on its forehead.

discovery.text: The Golem patrolled the ghetto at night, protecting Jewish homes from attackers with superhuman strength.

twist.text: The Golem grew violent. The rabbi erased one letter, changing 'emet' (truth) to 'met' (death), and it crumbled.

climax.text: The Golem story directly inspired Frankenstein, robots in fiction, and the concept of artificial intelligence ethics.

punchline.text: A clay giant from 1580 raised the same AI questions we ask today.

quiz.question: How did Rabbi Loew stop the Golem when it became dangerous?
options: He trapped it in a sealed underground chamber
He erased one letter from its forehead, changing 'truth' to 'death'
He performed a prayer that sent its spirit back to heaven
